correctness.rationale: For hub-absent faces the complex is B=*_{i=1}^k sk_{r-1} Delta(L_i); for hub-present faces it is the cone on K=sk_{r-2} Delta(L) with intersection K. This is an exact face equivalence for all r. When 2<=r<s, B is a (kr-2)-connected join of bouquets in degree kr-1 and dim K=r-2, so K->B is null and cofiber B wedge Sigma K. When s<=r<=ks, B is contractible; when r>=ks+1, hub cones off all. At r=1 isolated hub and joined discrete leaves give Htilde_0=Z and (s-1)^k spheres of dimension k-1. Standard augmented exterior-chain skeleton model gives Htilde_{r-1}=exterior^{r-1} U and mixed top tensor exterior^r U_i integrally and naturally; swapping two join factors of reduced degree r-1 yields sign (-1)^r. Independent direct induced-component mod-2 boundary ranks matched formulas for all 47 tested k,s,r triples; finite samples corroborate, not prove the general construction. Only ordinary wedge, not equivariant wedge equivalence.

value.rationale: A natural family of clique windmill block graphs has an explicit, nontrivial transition between single-degree and mixed-dimensional sphere wedges, plus full integral wreath-group representation lattices. These are topological and equivariant structural facts not mechanistically supplied by mere Betti counts; the precise r<s boundary is a useful motivated classification.

final_claim: For k,s>=2 and all integer r>=1, the higher independence complex of K1 join k disjoint K_s has the stated point/disconnected and one- or two-degree wedge homotopy classification; its integral Aut=S_s wreath S_k homology modules are exterior powers of augmentation kernels and a Koszul-twisted tensor product.
